newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX electric futures down in bearish mood.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX electric futures down in bearish mood.

text.p: NYMEX electricity futures were trading lower Wednesday as March contracts began their first day of front month trade amidst a bearish mood, industry sources said.
"There is a feeling that there is a lot of power out there, and March is a swing month," said one New York based futures trader, adding "there is just not a lot to prop these contracts up right now."
As of 1220 EST, March California Oregon Border (COB) had traded down 35 cents at $11.05 per megawatt hour (MWh) after hitting a new contract low of $11.00 and trading as high as $11.25 per MWh.
April COB had traded down 75 cents at a new contract low of $9.75 per MWh following trade as high as $10.00 per MWh.
March Palo Verde (PV) had traded down 30 cents at $13.30 after moving as low as $13.25, while April PV had traded down 25 cents at a new contract low of $12.25 and trade as high as $12.50 per MWh.

Traders said a bearish sentiment pervaded electricity trade, with power demand expected to wane as warmer spring weather approached and hydroelectric supply increased from melting Pacific Northwest snow.
Pressure was also seen on electricity from lower physical power prices and cheaper natural gas.
As of 1225 EST, March Henry Hub natural gas futures were trading down 4.1 cents at $2.505 per million British thermal units.

Bonneville Power Administration left its prices and volumes for Thursday delivery of surplus power unchanged from offers for Wednesday delivery, with up to 200 megawatts of firm power offered at $14.00 per MWh in the Northwest.
NYMEX said that as of 1155 EST, an estimated total of 16 COB and eight PV contracts had traded.
The Northwest is forecast to experience mild and very wet weather through the end of the week, while the Southwest is expected to stay warm and dry during the same period.
A 500 kilovolt transmission line, which runs from Snohomish County, Wash. to the Canadian border, could restart today after damage from an ice storm almost two weeks ago.
A 262 megawatt coal-fired unit at the Rawhide power plant in northern Colorado is expected resume operation today after being shut last Saturday for boiler tube repairs.
